subject: the published signal-flow graph in logic://mixer
question: What stops the routing graph from completing — node identity, or something else?

host.project: three plain audio tracks, no sends, default Stereo Out

reverify.command: Read logic://mixer and note routing_graph.nodes/edges/partialReason. Then read logic://tracks so trk_ references are issued, read logic://mixer again, and compare.
reverify.expected: nodes go from 0 to the track count once references exist; edges stay 0 with partialReason naming unreadable output destination endpoints
reverify.cost: ~1 min; needs a project with at least one track

method: Read logic://mixer before and after reading logic://tracks in the same session, so the effect of issuing trk_ references on the graph is observed rather than reasoned about. partialReason was read in full both times.

observations.partialReason_head: unresolved source endpoint for mixer strip track_index=0: no issued trk_ reference; unreadable output destination endpoint for source track_index=0
unreadable output destination endpoint for source track_index=0; unreadable output destination endpoint for source track_index=1; unreadable output destination endpoint for source track_index=2

observations.prior_decision: an edge is published only when both endpoints resolve to an already-issued reference; a display string is never promoted to a node identity

conclusion: The graph publishes and is honest about being partial. Node identity is settled and works: once logic://tracks issues trk_ references, nodes resolve from 0 to 3 and the 'no issued trk_ reference' clause disappears from partialReason. What remains is a different problem entirely — every edge is blocked by an unreadable output destination endpoint. ADR-008's row, which says node identity needs a decision, describes a question PR #740 already decided and shipped; the live blocker is reading the destination, not naming the node.
limits: Three plain audio tracks with no sends and default routing. A project with busses or sends may fail differently, and sends were measured on #291 to be the harder half.
Says only that the destination endpoint is unreadable in this state — not why, and not whether it is readable in another.
Node resolution was observed for tracks; whether every node CLASS (busses, aux, master) resolves the same way is unmeasured.
